raw_case_text: A 56-year-old male patient presented to the emergency department of the People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China, due to cough, fever and abdominal pain. The patient was diagnosed with abdominal infection and received intravenous injection of ceftriaxone for treatment. After 4 days, his condition was steadily deteriorated and he was admitted to the Department of Gastroenterology at our hospital. The patient had a history of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes and abuse of corticosteroids for the treatment of his reiterative gouty arthritis for 10 years, which resulted in secondary adrenal insufficiency. Currently, he takes prednisone acetate 20mg/d for the treatment of secondary adrenal insufficiency. A month ago, he inhaled air particles that had been contaminated during house renovation activities. The laboratory examination revealed leukocytosis (28.56 x 10^9/L), neutrophil ratio of 90.3%, C-reactive protein of >200 mg/L (normal values 0-5 mg/L), procalcitonin of 1.60 ng/mL (normal values 0-0.05 ng/mL), and poor glycemic control (Glu 8.95mmol/L, HbA1c 11.5%). The patient had recurrent fever with a maximum temperature of 39.1 C and a palpable mass in the lower abdomen. Pulmonary CT showed bilateral pneumonia, tracheal diverticulum, multiple bilateral rib old fractures and a small amount of pericardial effusion (Figure 1A). Abdominal CT indicated irregular nodular or slightly low-density shadows with multiple soft tissue densities in the right renal hilum, right retroperitoneal space, and right pelvic extraperitoneal space, with the largest of those locating in front of the right iliac muscle, measuring about 52mm x 38mm, suggesting infectious lesions and encapsulated effusion (Figure 1B). Brain CT demonstrated no abnormalities. Treatment included empirical anti-infection, active blood glucose control, oxygen therapy, and fluid replacement. Due to the seriousness of the patient's infection and the uncertainty regarding the presence of multi-drug resistant bacterial infection, imipenem/cilastatin (IPM/CS) was used without determination of a clear infectious etiology. Next day, the patient underwent invasive puncture drainage of the largest abscess located in front of the right iliac muscle under CT-guidance, and punctured milky yellow green pus was sent to microbiological examination. Meanwhile, blood cultures were taken. Gram staining of the puncture fluid showed elongated, branching Gram-positive bacteria, with beaded filamentous structures (Figure 2A), which was suspected actinomycosis. However, the modified acid-fast staining showed acid-fast thin branching bacterium, which highly suspected the presence of Nocardia infection (Figure 2B). Small, dry, wrinkled, pale yellow colonies appeared on the blood agar (Figure 2C) and examination of the colonies under a 10x objective lens showed abundant aerial hyphae on agar medium (Figure 2D), which was further dentified as N. farcinica by MALDI-TOF MS (Bruker, France, reference database version is V10 9607MSPs). The treatment plan was modified to include combination therapy with TMP-SMX (3 pieces every 8 hours, each piece containing 80 mg of trimethoprim and 400mg of sulfamethoxazole) and IPM/CS (1 g, every 8 hours), along with continuous drainage of the abdominal abscesses, and reduction the dosage of glucocorticoids. During hospitalization, no pathogens were found in blood and sputum cultures. After 27 days of treatment, the patient's temperature returned to normal, inflammatory markers significantly decreased (Figure 3A-D), and the abdominal abscesses were notably absorbed (Figure 3E), indicating improvement in the condition and the patient can be discharged. We advised the patient to continue oral TMP-SMX 3 pieces three times a day for 6-12 months.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 56-year-old male presented with cough, recurrent high fever (up to 39.1 C), and abdominal pain that worsened despite 4 days of intravenous ceftriaxone.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient initially presented to the emergency department with cough, fever, and abdominal pain, where he was diagnosed with an abdominal infection and treated with intravenous ceftriaxone for 4 days. Due to steady clinical deterioration and recurrent fever up to 39.1 C, he was admitted to the Department of Gastroenterology.
subjective.past_medical_history: Poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, recurrent gouty arthritis with a 10-year history of corticosteroid abuse resulting in secondary adrenal insufficiency (currently maintained on prednisone acetate 20 mg/day), and inhalation of contaminated dust particles during house renovation 1 month prior to presentation.

objective.physical_examination: Recurrent fever with maximum temperature of 39.1 C and a palpable mass in the lower abdomen.
objective.routine_investigations: Laboratory tests revealed marked leukocytosis (28.56 x 10^9/L) with 90.3% neutrophils, CRP >200 mg/L (reference: 0-5 mg/L), procalcitonin 1.60 ng/mL (reference: 0-0.05 ng/mL), blood glucose 8.95 mmol/L, and HbA1c 11.5%. Blood and sputum cultures remained negative throughout hospitalization.
objective.advanced_workup: Pulmonary CT showed bilateral pneumonia, a tracheal diverticulum, multiple old bilateral rib fractures, and a small pericardial effusion. Abdominal CT demonstrated irregular nodular and slightly low-density soft-tissue masses in the right renal hilum, right retroperitoneal space, and right pelvic extraperitoneal space—the largest anterior to the right iliacus muscle measuring 52 x 38 mm—consistent with infectious abscesses and encapsulated effusion. Brain CT was normal. CT-guided percutaneous puncture and drainage of the right iliacus abscess yielded milky yellow-green pus.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Retroperitoneal/iliopsoas and disseminated nocardiosis caused by Nocardia farcinica was confirmed: Gram stain of the aspirated pus showed elongated branching Gram-positive beaded filamentous rods, modified acid-fast stain showed acid-fast thin branching filaments, blood agar culture grew small, dry, wrinkled pale-yellow colonies with abundant aerial hyphae, and MALDI-TOF MS (Bruker V10 9607MSPs) identified Nocardia farcinica (ruling out actinomycosis). Empirical imipenem/cilastatin (IPM/CS) was combined with oral TMP-SMX (3 tablets of 80/400 mg every 8 hours) and IPM/CS (1 g every 8 hours), alongside continuous catheter drainage, glycemic control, and glucocorticoid dose reduction. After 27 days of treatment, fever resolved, inflammatory markers normalized, and repeat CT showed marked abscess absorption; he was discharged on oral TMP-SMX (3 tablets three times daily) for 6-12 months.
